subject: general
question: A dealer purchased a dryer for ₹92,000. He allows a discount of 77% on its marked price and still gains 83%. Find the marked price of the dryer.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct ratio formula between CP and MP:

CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%)

CP : MP = (100 − 77) : (100 + 83) = 23 : 183

Here, 23 units = ₹92,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹4,000

⇒ 183 units = 183 × 4,000 = ₹7,32,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,32,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹92,000

Discount % (D) = 77%

Profit % (P) = 83%

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × [(100 + P) ÷ (100 − D)]

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = 92000 × [(100 + 83) ÷ (100 − 77)]

⇒ MP = 92000 × (183 ÷ 23)

⇒ MP = 4000 × 183

⇒ MP = 7,32,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,32,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the article. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price, while Profit or Loss is calculated on the Cost Price.

Successive Discount

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are applied on an item, the equivalent single discount is given by: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

A seller who claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight gains a profit. Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
